examples.en: If you add up the scores for each item, you get the total score.
The total score for the exam is out of 100.
People with the higher total score get selected first.
Please calculate the total score of the two subjects.
Passing is decided by the total score.
I was five points short on the total score, so I failed.

explain: 여러 점수를 모두 더한 합계예요. 가능한 가장 높은 점수는 '만점'이라고 하니 총점과 헷갈리지 마세요. 점수를 사람 수나 과목 수로 나눈 값은 '평균'이에요.

phrases.en: The student with the highest total score gets a scholarship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수의 합계가 크다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the sum of scores is large.

phrases.en: I add up the scores for each subject to calculate the total.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 모두 더하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for adding up all the scores.

phrases.en: I got 180 out of a total of 200 points.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전체 점수와 받은 점수를 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the points you got out of the total.

explain_en: Added points across exam subjects (시험 총점) It's the sum of several scores. The highest possible score is '만점', so don't mix it up with 총점. The value divided by the number of people or subjects is '평균' (average).

examples.ko: 아이가 생기니까 학군을 보고 이사를 갔어요.
examples.en: After we had a child, we moved with the school district in mind.
This neighborhood is famous for its good schools.
House prices rose a lot because of the school district.

examples.ko: 학군이 같은 친구들끼리 한 학교에 모여요.
examples.en: Friends from the same district gather at one school.

examples.ko: 부모님은 좋은 학군에 사는 게 중요하다고 하세요.
examples.en: My parents say living in a good school district matters.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 학군이 달라서 그 학교에 못 가요.
examples.en: Our house is in a different district, so I can't go to that school.

explain: '학군이 좋다'는 부모가 이사할 집을 고를 때 많이 하는 말이에요. 좋은 학교가 모여 있는 곳은 '학군지'라고도 해요. 한국에서는 집값과 자주 같이 이야기해요.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a home in a good school district area so I can move there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 학교가 모인 지역을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an area where good schools are concentrated.

phrases.en: I want to live in a neighborhood with a good school district.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사할 곳을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about where to move.

phrases.en: I consider the school district when I choose a home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 조건 중에 학군을 꼼꼼히 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when carefully weighing the school district among other conditions.

explain_en: 학군이 좋다 is something parents say a lot when choosing where to move. An area with many good schools is also called 학군지. In Korea it is often discussed together with housing prices.

en: to change suddenly; to shift sharply

examples.en: The weather changed suddenly and rain poured down.

examples.ko: 기술이 급변하는 시대에는 계속 배워야 해요.
examples.en: In an age when technology changes rapidly, you have to keep learning.
His expression changed abruptly in an instant.

examples.ko: 시장 상황이 급변하면 계획도 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: If market conditions change suddenly, we have to change our plans too.
Nobody knew why the mood changed so suddenly.

examples.ko: 환자의 상태가 급변할 수 있으니 잘 지켜봐 주세요.
examples.en: The patient's condition could change suddenly, so please keep a close eye on him.

explain: '변하다'보다 변화가 갑작스럽고 크다는 느낌이 강해요. 날씨, 상황, 표정, 환자의 상태에 자주 쓰고, '급변하는 시대', '급변하는 세상'이 흔한 짝말이에요.

phrases.en: You must prepare to survive in a rapidly changing world.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급변하는'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common modifier form that describes the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The patient's condition changed suddenly at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 건강이 갑자기 나빠지거나 달라질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's health suddenly shifts.

phrases.en: The plan suddenly changed, so I was flustered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '급변하다' 대신 쉽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to '급변하다'.

explain_en: Fast change in situation or weather — neutral, written. Compared with '변하다', it strongly suggests the change is sudden and big. It is often used for weather, situations, expressions and a patient's condition. Common pairings are '급변하는 시대' and '급변하는 세상'.

t90.ax: Nobody knew why the mood changed so suddenly.

en: foot of a mountain; base of a hill; riverbank

examples.ko: 산 밑 기슭에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple at the foot of the mountain.

examples.ko: 눈이 녹아서 언덕 기슭에 꽃이 피었어요.
examples.en: The snow melted and flowers bloomed at the foot of the hill.

examples.ko: 마을은 한라산 기슭을 따라 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: The village stretches long along the foot of Hallasan.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 저쪽 기슭이 붉게 물들어요.
examples.en: When the sun sets, the foot of the slope over there turns red.
Reeds are growing along the lake's edge.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 기슭 마을이 위험해졌어요.
examples.en: With so much rain, the village at the slope's foot became dangerous.

explain: '산기슭'처럼 산이나 언덕이 끝나는 아래쪽 부분에 써요. 위쪽은 '산꼭대기'나 '정상', 가운데는 '산허리'예요. 강이나 바다의 가장자리는 '기슭'보다 '강가', '바닷가'가 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.en: My house is at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산'과 붙여 한 낱말로 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, written as one word with 산.

phrases.en: We ate lunch at the foot of the hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이 아닌 낮은 언덕의 아래쪽에도 '기슭'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 기슭 also works for the bottom of a smaller hill.

phrases.en: I sat on the riverbank and looked at the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강의 가장자리를 말해요. 일상에서는 '강가'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the edge of a river; 강가 is more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is used like '산기슭' for the lower part where a mountain or hill ends. The top is '산꼭대기' or '정상', and the middle is '산허리'. For river or sea edges, '강가' and '바닷가' are more everyday than '기슭'.

examples.en: There is a jujube tree in the yard of my grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 대추나무에 열매가 빨갛게 익어요.
examples.en: In autumn, the fruit on the jujube tree ripens red.
Children are playing under the jujube tree.

examples.ko: 이 대추나무는 올해 열매가 많이 열렸어요.
examples.en: This jujube tree bore a lot of fruit this year.
We planted a jujube tree in the yard.

examples.ko: 대추나무 가지에 가시가 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The jujube tree's branches have thorns, so you have to be careful.

explain: 대추가 열리는 나무예요. 대추는 차나 한방 재료, 명절 음식에 많이 써요. 옛날이야기나 속담에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 그는 대추나무 연 걸리듯 빚이 여기저기 있어요.
phrases.en: He has debts here and there, like kites hanging all over a jujube tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빚이 여기저기 많이 걸려 있는 모양을 말해요. 가지에 연이 잔뜩 걸린 모습에 빗댄 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone with debts scattered everywhere, comparing it to kites snagged all over the branches.
phrases.en_equiv: be up to one's neck in debt

explain_en: It is the tree that bears jujubes. Jujubes are widely used in tea, herbal medicine and holiday food. The tree also appears in old tales and proverbs.

examples.en: Bears hibernate in caves during winter.
I heard frogs also hibernate underground.
Squirrels gather acorns before they hibernate.
Snakes go into hibernation when the weather gets cold.

examples.ko: 동면하는 동물은 겨울에 먹이를 거의 먹지 않아요.
examples.en: Animals that hibernate hardly eat in winter.
When spring comes, the bears that hibernated wake up.

explain: '동면하다'는 동물이 추운 겨울에 오랫동안 자는 것을 말해요. '겨울잠을 자다'가 훨씬 자주 쓰이는 말이고, '동면'은 과학 설명에서 더 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: Bears sleep through the winter in a den.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동면하다'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '동면하다' and more common in daily speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to hibernate (lit. sleep the winter sleep)

phrases.en: When the weather gets cold, frogs go into hibernation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동면을 시작하는 순간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the moment an animal begins hibernating.

phrases.example: 동면하는 동물은 겨울 전에 많이 먹어요.
phrases.en: Animals that hibernate eat a lot before winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 동물을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-는' to describe which animals do this.

explain_en: 동면하다 means an animal sleeping for a long time in the cold winter. '겨울잠을 자다' is used far more often, and 동면 appears more in science explanations.

examples.en: I saw fireflies for the first time on a summer night in the countryside.
Fireflies twinkled among the grass.

examples.ko: 깨끗한 개울가에서만 반딧불이를 볼 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard you can only see fireflies by clean streams.
The kids took part in a firefly experience event.
Fireflies give off light from their tails.
The firefly lights looked like stars.

explain: '반딧불이'는 곤충 이름이고, '이'까지가 한 단어라서 '반딧불이가', '반딧불이를'처럼 조사가 붙으면 '이'가 겹쳐 보여요. '반딧불'은 그 곤충이 내는 불빛을 가리켜요. 곤충은 '개똥벌레'라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: Grandmother calls fireflies 'gaeddong-beolle'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 곤충을 부르는 다른 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same insect.

phrases.en: Fireflies fly on summer nights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반딧불이가 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes fireflies moving through the air.

phrases.en: We go to see fireflies on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하러 가는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for going somewhere to watch fireflies.

explain_en: Standard everyday name for the firefly in speech and textbooks. This is the name of the insect, and the final '이' is part of the word, so with particles it looks like '반딧불이가' or '반딧불이를', with the '이' appearing twice. '반딧불' refers to the light the insect gives off. The insect is also called '개똥벌레'.

examples.en: The snow squeaked when I stepped on it.
I scrubbed the plate until it squeaked, and now it sparkles.

examples.ko: 깨끗이 씻은 그릇에서 뽀드득 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The well-washed bowl makes a squeaky sound.
The kids walk along crunching through the snow.

examples.ko: 체육관 바닥에서 운동화가 뽀드득 소리를 내요.
examples.en: Sneakers squeak on the gym floor.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침에 뽀드득 눈 밟는 소리가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like the crunch of stepping on snow on a winter morning.

explain: 쌓인 눈을 밟을 때나 깨끗이 씻은 물건을 문지를 때 나는 소리예요. 소리가 반복되면 '뽀드득뽀드득'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I walked along the snowy path, crunching with every step.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 반복될 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the squeaking sound repeats.

phrases.example: 눈을 밟을 때 뽀드득 소리가 나서 기분이 좋아요.
phrases.en: I like the crunching sound when I step on snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 명사처럼 설명할 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The way to describe the sound as a noun phrase.

phrases.en: I scrubbed my hands squeaky clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗이 씻겨서 소리가 날 정도라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests it is washed so clean that it squeaks.

explain_en: Squeaky crunch of snow or clean rubbing; light, clean sound. It is the sound of stepping on packed snow or rubbing something that has been washed clean. When the sound repeats, you say '뽀드득뽀드득'.

examples.en: I went to the arboretum with my family on the weekend.

examples.ko: 이 수목원에는 사계절 다른 꽃이 피어요.
examples.en: Different flowers bloom here in the arboretum in every season.

examples.ko: 가을에는 단풍이 예쁜 수목원이 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: In autumn, arboretums with beautiful fall leaves are popular.
I took a slow walk inside the arboretum.

examples.ko: 수목원 입장권은 인터넷으로 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy arboretum tickets online.
I observed insects with my child at the arboretum.

explain: '공원'은 쉬고 노는 곳이고, '수목원'은 여러 나무와 식물을 모아 키우며 보여 주는 곳이에요. '식물원'은 주로 온실에서 키우는 식물을 보여 줘요. 발음은 [수모권]처럼 이어서 소리 나요.

phrases.en: I walked slowly around the arboretum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수목원에서 가장 흔한 활동이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common activity there.
phrases.en_equiv: to take a walk in the arboretum

phrases.en: The national arboretum has many big trees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라에서 운영하는 큰 수목원을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A large arboretum run by the state.

phrases.en: At a botanical garden you see warm greenhouse plants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수목원과 달리 주로 온실의 식물을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike an arboretum, it mostly shows greenhouse plants.

explain_en: A 공원 is for resting and playing, while a 수목원 collects and grows many kinds of trees and plants for people to see. A 식물원 mostly shows plants grown in greenhouses. It is pronounced with linking, like [수모권].

examples.en: Many migratory birds come to this wetland.

examples.ko: 습지는 물이 잘 빠지지 않는 땅이에요.
examples.en: A wetland is land where water does not drain easily.
People who protect wetlands gathered.
I looked at the reeds at the Suncheon Bay wetland.
The path led into a wetland, so my shoes got wet.
It was a class to observe the plants and insects of the wetland.

explain: 습지는 환경과 자연 보호 이야기에서 쓰는 말이고, '늪'은 더 깊고 빠질 것 같은 곳을 말해요. '갯벌'은 바다 가까이에서 밀물과 썰물 때 드러나는 땅이라 달라요.

phrases.example: 우리 동네는 습지 보호 활동을 해요.
phrases.en: Our town does activities to protect the wetland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 이야기에서 습지와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The phrase most often used with 습지 in talk about the environment.

phrases.en: This bird lives in the wetland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이나 식물이 사는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where an animal or plant lives.

phrases.en: There is deep water in a swamp, so it's dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '습지'보다 더 깊고 위험한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels deeper and more dangerous than 습지.

explain_en: 습지 is the word used in talk about the environment and nature protection, while 늪 is a deeper place where you might sink. 갯벌 is different: it is the land near the sea that is exposed at low tide.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 산에 야생화가 활짝 피어요.
examples.en: In spring, wildflowers bloom all over the mountains.
I took a photo of the wildflowers blooming by the road.
Seoraksan is famous for its wildflower fields.

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 정원 꽃이 아니라 야생화예요.
examples.en: This isn't a garden flower; it's a wildflower.
I walked slowly through a field full of wildflowers.

examples.ko: 야생화 이름을 알려 주는 앱이 있어요.
examples.en: There's an app that tells you the names of wildflowers.

explain: 사람이 심지 않아도 산과 들에서 저절로 자라는 꽃이에요. '들꽃'과 거의 같은 뜻인데, 일상에서는 '들꽃'이 더 부드럽게 들리고 '야생화'는 안내문이나 설명에서 잘 보여요.

phrases.en: The wildflowers have bloomed beautifully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같고 일상 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning and sounds softer in conversation.

phrases.en: I went to the wildflower festival on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 보러 가는 행사 이름에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the names of flower-viewing events.

phrases.en: Taking wildflower photos is my hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 찍거나 보여 줄 때 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when photographing or showing flowers.

explain_en: Sino-Korean, slightly formal; hiking, nature and botany contexts. These are flowers that grow by themselves in mountains and fields without being planted. It is nearly the same as '들꽃', but '들꽃' sounds softer in daily talk, while '야생화' appears more in signs and explanations.

t90.ax: Seoraksan is famous for its wildflower fields.

examples.en: Heat haze shimmered up into the air.
The ripples glimmer on the water.

examples.ko: 불빛이 어른어른 보여서 가까이 가 봤어요.
examples.en: A light flickered faintly, so I went closer.

examples.ko: 더운 날 길 위로 열기가 어른어른 올라와요.
examples.en: On a hot day, heat shimmers up from the road.
The letters wavered in front of my eyes.
The shadows sway and flicker in the candlelight.

explain: 빛, 그림자, 열기처럼 흔들리며 희미하게 보이는 것 앞에 써요. '보이다', '흔들리다', '비치다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Lights shimmered faintly on the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이나 그림자가 흔들리며 희미하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when light or shadow appears faintly and wavering.

phrases.en: I can faintly make out a person in the distance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멀거나 흐려서 확실히 안 보이는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something far or blurry that isn't clearly visible.

phrases.en: The candle flame wavers and flickers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불꽃이나 열기가 가볍게 흔들리는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a flame or heat haze swaying lightly.

explain_en: It is used before things that look faint and unsteady, like light, shadows or heat. It goes well with verbs like '보이다', '흔들리다' and '비치다'.

t90.ax: The ripples glimmer on the water.

examples.en: Rain is forecast across the country tomorrow.
Snow has been forecast for the weekend.
A typhoon was forecast, so I put off my trip.
The rain started earlier than the forecast time.

examples.ko: 한파가 예보될 때는 옷을 따뜻하게 입어요.
examples.en: When a cold wave is forecast, I dress warmly.
Strong winds are forecast from the afternoon.

explain: 예보되다는 날씨나 재해가 미리 알려졌다는 뜻으로 주로 날씨 뉴스에서 써요. '비가 예보되어 있다', '폭설이 예보됐다'처럼 날씨 말과 같이 나와요. 사람이 일부러 알리는 건 '예보하다', 알려진 결과를 말하는 건 예보되다예요.

phrases.example: 일기 예보에서 내일 눈이 온다고 했어요.
phrases.en: The weather forecast said it will snow tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨를 미리 알려 주는 방송이나 소식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The broadcast or news that announces the weather in advance.

phrases.en: A typhoon is forecast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 알려진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state that has already been announced.

phrases.en: This snow wasn't forecast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 미리 알려지지 않았을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form for weather that was not predicted.

explain_en: Yebodoeda is used mostly in weather news for something that has been announced ahead of time, as in 비가 예보되어 있다. 예보하다 is the person or agency doing the announcing, while 예보되다 describes the result that has been announced. It sits next to weather words such as rain, snow, and typhoon.

examples.en: Seoul's latitude is about 37 degrees north.

examples.ko: 위도가 높은 나라일수록 겨울 낮이 짧아요.
examples.en: The higher a country's latitude, the shorter its winter days.

examples.ko: 지도에서 위도와 경도를 찾아 위치를 확인했어요.
examples.en: I found the latitude and longitude on the map and checked the location.
The equator is the line at zero degrees latitude.

examples.ko: 같은 위도에 있어도 바다와 가까우면 기온이 달라요.
examples.en: Even at the same latitude, the temperature differs if you are near the sea.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 위도가 낮아서 겨울에도 따뜻해요.
examples.en: This city is at a low latitude, so it's warm even in winter.

explain: 짝말은 '경도'이고, 지도에서 가로로 그은 선으로 적도를 기준으로 북위와 남위를 나눠요. '위도가 높다/낮다'처럼 쓰고, 지리 수업이나 날씨 설명에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I checked the latitude and longitude on the map.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝말인 '경도'와 함께 위치를 말할 때 늘 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Always appears with its partner 경도 when giving a location.

phrases.example: 고위도 지역은 겨울에 낮이 아주 짧아요.
phrases.en: In high-latitude regions, winter days are very short.
phrases.nuance_ko: 적도에서 멀리 떨어진 북쪽이나 남쪽 지역을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to regions far from the equator, to the north or south.

phrases.example: 적도 근처는 위도가 낮아서 일 년 내내 더워요.
phrases.en: Near the equator the latitude is low, so it's hot all year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 적도에 가까운 곳을 말할 때 '위도가 낮다'고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Places near the equator are described as having low latitude.

explain_en: Its partner word is '경도' (longitude). Latitude lines run horizontally on a map and are divided into north and south of the equator. You say '위도가 높다/낮다', and it comes up in geography lessons and weather explanations.
